target: Azoth session-closeout and scope-gate lifecycle design
summary: Repeated closeout confusion suggests an architectural boundary issue between session-closeout state, scope-gate state, pipeline-gate state, and already-closed session detection.
evidence: After the deploy parity fix was administratively finalized, `$azoth-session-closeout` correctly soft-stopped because `.azoth/scope-gate.json` was closed, `.azoth/session-gate.json` was closed, run-ledger had no active run, and ep-354 already recorded closeout. However, the operator still had to reason across multiple artifacts to know whether closeout should run, soft-stop, or create duplicate W1 state. The prior T-KRP-C planning repair also exposed that stale pipeline-gate/scope-gate residue can create mismatch noise when opening a new ad-hoc scope. These are symptoms of lifecycle authority being distributed across files without a single operator-facing session lifecycle resolver.
recommended_action: Design a first-class session lifecycle resolver that computes one authoritative state from scope-gate, pipeline-gate, session-gate, run-ledger, session-state, and latest closeout episode. It should classify states such as live delivery, live exploratory, already closed, partially closed, stale gate residue, and no active session; then route closeout/start/next behavior from that resolver instead of each command re-deriving lifecycle truth independently.
